articles.title: We Deliver
articles.summary: On the evening of October 9, 1998, an amateur astronomer, Jay Freeman, recounts a humorous attempt to share a view through his Vixen 70mm fluorite telescope with a date. Despite her initial playful reluctance, mimicking a two-year-old patient, and declaring she didn't want to look at Saturn because she'd seen better pictures, the astronomer gently tried to persuade her to trust him. The setup was strategically placed to ensure observation.

articles.title: SJAA Activities Calendar
articles.summary: The SJAA Activities Calendar details upcoming events for December and January, including general meetings, numerous star parties at various locations like Houge Park, Fremont Peak, and Coe, and an Observational Astronomy class. Key highlights include a general meeting featuring a NASA planetary scientist discussing Europa and multiple opportunities for night sky observation.

articles.title: Sperling Is Sterling
articles.summary: Norm Sperling gave a talk titled "Oxyronic Astronomy" at an SJAA indoor astronomy event, challenging confusing terminology in the field. He highlighted paradoxes and misleading terms like 'waning crescent,' 'blackbody radiation,' 'forbidden lines,' and the 'Hubble Constant,' questioning how students can grasp these concepts. The entertaining and thought-provoking presentation aimed to clarify the inconsistencies in astronomical language.

articles.title: The Celestial Tourist Speaks
articles.summary: Jay Freeman recounts a successful weekend observing trip to Pacheco State Park in October 1998, highlighting the site's dark skies despite initial wind issues. Using his Celestron 14, he observed numerous galaxies, M31's G1 globular cluster, and enjoyed improved seeing on Saturday for detailed views of Jupiter and Saturn. The article also includes a charming anecdote about sharing a view of Saturn with a date, emphasizing the joy of sharing astronomy.

articles.title: Akkana Peck
articles.summary: This article provides an observational guide for December, detailing the visibility and key features of planets like Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. It highlights Mercury's morning apparition, Mars's growing disk, and a notable event where Mars will pass near the carbon star SS Virginis, inviting observers to note the color contrast. Jupiter and Saturn are well-placed for evening observation, with specific phenomena like Jupiter's quadrature and Saturn's temporary ring tilt also mentioned.

articles.title: David North
articles.summary: December is identified as a favorable month for lunar observation, particularly due to the moon's high elevation after the full moon. This period offers exceptional views of eastern terminator features like Mare Crisium and the "Gang Of Four" craters (Langrenus, Vandelinus, Petavius, Furnerius), allowing for detailed inspection of their unique characteristics, including rimae and secondary crater fields. The article also highlights other features like Atlas, Hercules, Endymion, and Vallis Rheita, noting that the week between Christmas and New Year will be excellent for general lunar viewing, provided clear weather.

articles.title: David North
articles.summary: This article provides details on the Geminid and Ursid meteor showers, describing the Geminids as the strongest annual shower, peaking on Dec 13/14 with ideal moonless conditions in 1998, and identifying Asteroid 3200 Phaethon as its parent body. It also covers the weaker Ursids, visible around Dec 21/22, linked to comet 8p/Tuttle, and mentions a potential strong display in 2000.

articles.title: Bill Arnett
articles.summary: This document summarizes a board meeting where directors approved past minutes and discussed several key organizational matters. Terry Kahl's resignation necessitates a special election procedure for her replacement, and Doug Davis was announced as the instructor for the upcoming astronomy class. Additionally, Dave North is transitioning Ephemeris editing duties to Jane Houston and Morris Jones, and updates were provided on the treasurer's report and the loaner program.

articles.title: Directions to SJAA places
articles.summary: This document provides detailed driving directions to four park locations frequently used for astronomical events and observation in the San Jose area. It offers specific instructions for Houge Park, Henry Coe State Park, Fremont Peak State Park, and Grant Ranch County Park, including notes on entrance fees and designated SJAA observation sites. These directions are essential for navigating to star parties and other gatherings hosted by the San Jose Astronomical Association and related groups.

articles.title: Jane Houston
articles.summary: On October 18, the author, Jane Houston, participated in a dark sky observing session at Fiddletown, utilizing her new 17.5-inch LITEBOX reflector. The session focused on deep-sky objects, particularly globular clusters within M31, M32, NGC 205, and M33, along with other nebulae and clusters. The experience was highly successful and fulfilling, leaving the author enthusiastic about future observing sessions.

articles.title: Sperling
articles.summary: This article, titled 'Sperling,' recounts humorous anecdotes from an astronomy class quiz, sharing several amusing student responses. It also describes a social gathering of an astronomy club at an all-night diner due to cloudy weather, where members discussed the SJAA Astronomical Pocket Diary and shared stories.

articles.title: Rich Neuschaffer
articles.summary: The article details a discussion between an amateur astronomer and Chief Ranger Paula Peterson of Monterey District Parks regarding issues at "the Peak." While a proposed gate installation was deemed problematic due to its impact on group campgrounds and other technical challenges, Ms. Peterson expressed strong support for amateur astronomers. She plans to collaborate with groups like FPOA, SJAA, and TAC to enhance the Peak as an astronomy site, addressing security concerns and potentially developing an astronomy-themed visitor center.

articles.title: David North
articles.summary: The article discusses significant changes, including the potential departure of Ranger Mike from Fremont Peak and the editor (David North) transitioning to a publisher role for the Ephemeris. A new editorial team, MoJane (Jane Houston and Morris Jones), will take over day-to-day editing. The issue also features an article by Rich Neuschaffer on Fremont Peak issues and a story by Jay Freeman.

articles.title: Activities Through Other Clubs
articles.summary: The article details astronomical activities available through other clubs, primarily TAC and PAS. TAC offers Wednesday night viewing at the Montebello site, requiring a permit holder, while PAS hosts public viewing at Foothill Observatory on clear Friday evenings and solar viewing on clear Saturday mornings. The document also lists specific December dates for PAS's annual meeting, board elections, and board meeting.

articles.title: School Star Parties
articles.summary: This article announces the schedule for upcoming school star parties in December, including a few in late November, and calls for volunteers to assist with these events. It emphasizes the importance and success of the San Jose Astronomical Association's star party program, sharing anecdotes from recent events that engaged hundreds of students with views of celestial objects like the Moon, Jupiter, and Saturn. Volunteers are asked to contact Jim Van Nuland for details and to verify event status.

articles.title: Candidates For Next Year
articles.summary: The nominating committee for the upcoming SJAA board of directors election has been formed, and several individuals have expressed interest in running. There are at least six seats up for election, including one due to a resignation, and the committee is seeking more candidates to ensure a competitive election. Members can qualify by a year of membership or six board meetings attended, with the election scheduled for the February meeting.

articles.title: Celestial Calendar
articles.summary: This Celestial Calendar provides an ephemeris for December 1998, detailing lunar phases and the positions of visible planets. It includes rise, transit, and set times, magnitudes, and celestial coordinates (RA/Dec) for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. The calendar also offers information on hours of darkness, astronomical twilight, sidereal time, and identifies the darkest Saturday night for observation.

articles.title: Don Machholz
articles.summary: This article provides an update on several active comets, detailing their current visibility, brightness, and orbital characteristics. It also lists recent comet discoveries, including C/1998 T1 (LINEAR), C/1998 S1 (LINEAR-Mueller), and others, often noting their discoverers and discovery methods. The piece concludes by highlighting amateur astronomers eligible for the Wilson Comet award for their varying discovery techniques.

articles.title: Ephemerides – Epoch 2000, 0h UTC
articles.summary: This document provides astronomical ephemerides for six comets, including 21P/Giacobini-Zinner, C/1997 J2 (Meunier-Dupouy), C/1998 P1 (Williams), C/1998 M5 (Linear), 88P/Howell, and C/1998 U5 (Linear). The data, specified for Epoch 2000, 0h UTC, details their Right Ascension, Declination, elongation, sky visibility (evening/morning), and apparent magnitude. It covers a period from December 3rd to January 2nd, serving as a guide for observers.

articles.title: Orbital Elements -- Epoch 2000.0
articles.summary: This document presents a table detailing orbital elements for six celestial objects, including comets such as Giacobini-Zinner and LINEAR, all referenced to Epoch 2000.0. For each object, specific astronomical data like perihelion date and distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, orbital period, and absolute magnitude are provided. This information appears to be part of an ephemeris for December 1998, likely intended for astronomical observation planning.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the current officers and members of the Board of Directors for an organization. It identifies individuals holding key positions such as President, Vice President, Secretary, and Treasurer, along with several Directors, providing a contact number for each. It serves as a directory for the organization's leadership.

articles.title: Ephemeris Staff
articles.summary: This document lists the staff contacts and their respective roles for "Ephemeris" and related organizational programs. It includes key personnel for editorial, circulation, printing, and chairpersons for various initiatives such as mentoring, observational astronomy, observatory committee, school star parties, and a telescope loaner program, along with a web page contact.

articles.title: Submit
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is inviting its members to submit articles for publication in the SJAA Ephemeris. Interested members should email their submissions to Dave North at Timocharis@aol.com.

articles.title: Astro Ads
articles.summary: This document is an advertisement listing several used astronomical items for sale. Items include an 80mm widefield refractor telescope with accessories, 9x63 Orion roof prism binoculars, and 8x42 Adlerblick binoculars, each with a price. Interested buyers are directed to contact Daniel Stokes in Salinas via phone.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Program Status
articles.summary: The Telescope Loaner Program is currently active and available to all members of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). Members interested in utilizing this program can contact Mike Koop directly via phone for more information and to arrange a loan.

articles.title: Current Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document lists telescopes currently on loan from an organization, detailing the scope type, borrower, and due date. It also informs interested parties about a waiting list policy for borrowing these scopes once they become available.

articles.title: Extended Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document lists astronomical telescopes whose loan periods have been extended, making them available for potential transfer to new borrowers. Interested individuals can inquire about borrowing these scopes, and the organization will coordinate a transfer time with the current borrower. The list includes various telescope types like Dobsons, a Refractor, and a C-11 Compustar.

articles.title: Available Scopes
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers a variety of telescopes for immediate loan to its members, stored at various members' homes. Interested individuals can contact Mike Koop to arrange for pickup at any listed SJAA event.

articles.title: Waiting List
articles.summary: Mike Koop is looking for storage space for one or more telescopes, specifically mentioning a "23 6" Newt/ P Mount Al Case." He provides contact information for individuals who might have available storage space.

articles.title: Periodical Publication Statement
articles.summary: The document serves as a periodical publication statement for the "SJAA Ephemeris," the official newsletter of the San Jose Astronomical Association. It confirms that the newsletter is published monthly, 12 times a year, from January through December. The statement also provides the mailing address for the San Jose Astronomical Association.

articles.title: To Subscribe to/Unsubscribe from the SJAA Mailing List send email to:
articles.summary: This document provides instructions on how to subscribe to or unsubscribe from the SJAA mailing list. Users need to send an email to sjaa-request@seds.org with a blank subject line and either "subscribe" or "unsubscribe" as the sole text in the email body. This information was published in the SJAA Ephemeris in December 1998.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), outlining membership fees ($15 for regular, $6 for junior) and an optional Sky & Telescope subscription add-on ($27). It provides instructions for submitting the form and payment (checks payable to SJAA) to the treasurer via mail or at a meeting, along with contact details and a mailing address.
